paper-estimation-local-time-varying-2022.summary: This paper develops a Bayesian hierarchical framework to correct bias in the local time-varying reproduction number when surveillance data misclassify imported versus local COVID-19 cases, validated via simulation and outbreaks in Hong Kong and Victoria, Australia. In discussing how to convert qualitative confidence judgments about case origin into numerical values, the authors cite Patki et al.'s Synthetic Data Vault as an example of a method that converts categorical variables to numerical data for Gaussian distribution. The SDV paper is only cited in passing as prior art for categorical-to-numerical transformation, not run or implemented in this work.

paper-generative-adversarial-network-aug.summary: This paper proposes a custom GAN (RNN/Bi-LSTM generator with a CNN discriminator) to augment a small experimental dataset (75 samples) for training a machine-learning model that improves instantaneous microwave frequency measurement accuracy in a photonic system. The GAN is bespoke to the authors' signal data and is not built on any SDV-family code. The paper cites the TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) only once, in a general remark about insufficient training data and the general notion of GANs, without engaging with its tabular-synthesis method.
paper-generative-adversarial-network-aug.needs: No full text available; cannot confirm whether TGAN's specific architecture was ever engaged with beyond a generic GAN citation.

paper-textbrew-automl-text-2022.summary: Builds an AutoML system for text classification that predicts which model family will win on a new dataset from cheap meta-features, then tunes and ensembles the winners, sidestepping the cost of trying every transformer. The meta-model's training data is the bottleneck, because public text-classification datasets are scarce, and CopulaGAN fills it: the SDV synthesizer generates 150 meta-dataset rows per candidate-model group, keeping the meta-dataset balanced.

paper-hybrid-over-under-sampling-2022.summary: An experimental study of which ORDER to combine under-sampling and over-sampling for class imbalanced data, run over 44 KEEL benchmark datasets with three over-sampling algorithms (SMOTE, CTGAN and TGAN) and three instance-selection algorithms (IB3, DROP3 and GA), scored by AUC under C4.5 and random forest classifiers. The headline finding is that instance selection carries most of the benefit: with IB3 chosen as the under-sampler, adding an over-sampling step brings no significant further improvement, and where both steps are required on large or extremely imbalanced data, instance selection first and over-sampling second is the better order. The paper is in the index because CTGAN is one of the three over-sampling algorithms actually executed rather than merely cited: section 4.4.2 and table 6 report random forest AUC for CTGAN alone, for CTGAN followed by IB3 and for IB3 followed by CTGAN, with the last of these tying for the highest rate reported anywhere in the paper, and the authors conclude that performing IB3 first is a stable procedure that makes different over-sampling methods produce similar results. CTGAN and TGAN are introduced as the tabular GAN variants proposed to generate discrete and continuous variables simultaneously, so the entry records both as generators the paper runs inside a comparison whose subject is the combination order rather than the generators themselves.

paper-word2vec-categorical-2022.summary: Proposes embedding categorical columns with Word2Vec so that generators restricted to numerical data can handle mixed tables at all. CTGAN's own categorical encoding is the comparison the proposal is measured against, so the paper is a direct challenge to how mode-specific normalization treats discrete columns.

paper-heavy-tailed-distribution-generati.summary: This paper proposes HTGAN, a generative adversarial network for industrial heavy-tailed data, in which the hidden variable z is drawn from a T distribution instead of Gaussian to better model fault data from the Tennessee Eastman (TE) process. The model is compared against a traditional GAN baseline on this synthetic fault-data generation task. CTGAN is cited only once in passing, in a remark about how industrial data differs from image data, and is not implemented or benchmarked.
paper-heavy-tailed-distribution-generati.needs: Full text not available; only the abstract and citing sentence fragment were seen, so it is unconfirmed whether CTGAN is discussed further in the body.

paper-biked-dataset-computational-bicycl.summary: This paper introduces BIKED, a dataset of 4500 individually designed bicycle models with parametric, image, and class-label data, intended to support data-driven design research. The authors explore the design space via unsupervised embeddings, train classifiers to interpret designs, and test Variational Autoencoders for generating new bicycle designs. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an alternative generative approach (GANs) to the VAEs actually used, without being run or evaluated.

paper-fake-till-you-make-2021.summary: This paper empirically investigates how data pre-processing, hyperparameter tuning, and iterative model-sharing settings affect the utility of synthetic data and the machine learning models trained on it, using propensity score and classification accuracy as utility measures across 15 datasets. It compares four synthetic data generation techniques: a Bayesian network method, a parametric method, a non-parametric tree-based method, and the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV). SDV is run as one of the four synthesizers evaluated, described as modeling the population's distribution via a latent Gaussian copula, with its propensity and accuracy results analyzed and contrasted against the others.

paper-reply-rc1-2021.summary: A peer-review response document accompanying a paper that explores copula-based statistical models for augmenting scarce training data used to build machine-learning emulators of physical processes, demonstrated on a toy longwave-radiation model. The associated abstract reports that copula-augmented synthetic data reduced mean absolute error by up to 62% relative to a baseline neural-network emulator. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper in connection with copula-based synthetic data generation, without evidence in the extracted text of running SDV software directly.
paper-reply-rc1-2021.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and metadata available. Cannot confirm whether SDV software (e.g. its GaussianCopula synthesizer) was actually run or merely cited as prior work on copula-based synthetic data.

paper-reply-rc2-2021.summary: This is an open-review reply accompanying a Geoscientific Model Development discussion paper that explores whether copula-based statistical models can generate synthetic data to augment scarce training sets for machine-learning emulators, tested on a toy physical model of downwelling longwave radiation. The augmented datasets substantially improved a neural-network emulator's accuracy (mean absolute error reduced by up to 62%). The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper in connection with copula-based synthetic data generation, without evidence in the available text that SDV's own code was run.

paper-syngen-2021.summary: Describes a platform for generating datasets on demand, aimed at practising data-science techniques without exposing real samples. It is assembled from two pieces: Faker for identifier-shaped columns and a Gaussian copula for the statistical structure, the same split SDV makes between fabricated fields and fitted distributions.

paper-additive-input-doubling-method-202.summary: This paper proposes an additive input-doubling method for small-data prediction tasks, combining a training-free data augmentation procedure with nonlinear SVR to boost prediction accuracy on short and very short datasets across domains such as medicine, economics, and materials science. It compares its approach against other data-augmentation and learning methods for small datasets. CTGAN is cited only in passing as prior work described as 'a new numerical data generator based on the training of GAN,' with no evidence it was run or benchmarked.

paper-brief-overview-methods-synthetic-2.summary: This report surveys methods for generating synthetic data for official statistics, aimed at Statistics Norway and other national statistics institutes, to enable safe and efficient data sharing while preserving both information value and privacy. It summarizes key references in the field, describing relational and deep-learning approaches to synthetic data generation. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) is described as a general synthetic data generator for relational databases, and CTGAN is mentioned among deep-learning-based synthetic data methods, both cited only as prior work rather than run.
paper-brief-overview-methods-synthetic-2.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentences available, so depth of engagement with SDV/CTGAN beyond brief description cannot be confirmed.

paper-combined-oversampling-undersamplin.summary: This paper proposes COUSS, a combined oversampling-undersampling algorithm inspired by TCP slow-start congestion control, designed to address class imbalance in network intrusion detection datasets such as KDD99. The method is evaluated against SMOTE, borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, and GAN-based oversampling, showing improved F1 scores. In its related-work discussion the paper describes Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN) and its use of variational Gaussian mixture mode-specific normalization to handle structured data, citing it as prior art rather than running the SDV-family library itself.
paper-combined-oversampling-undersamplin.needs: The abstract's 'generative adversarial network oversampling algorithm' baseline is not explicitly identified as CTGAN; unclear if CTGAN itself was ever executed rather than just described.

paper-date-2020.summary: This paper introduces DATE, a Dual-task Attentive Tree-aware Embedding model that combines tree-based feature extraction with dual attention mechanisms to classify and rank illicit customs trade transactions and predict associated tax revenue, evaluated on five years of real customs import data and discussed for deployment with the Nigeria Customs Service and World Customs Organization. In one supplementary experiment on the effect of tree number in the GBDT component, the authors note in a footnote that CTGAN was used for synthetic data generation, apparently to substitute for confidential real transaction data. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional GAN, is thus run as a data-generation tool for a single ancillary experiment rather than as part of the core fraud-detection pipeline.
paper-date-2020.needs: The extracted footnote conflicts with the stated finding that no SDV term appears outside the reference list; it is unclear how central or extensive the CTGAN-generated synthetic data was to the paper's broader experiments beyond this one figure.

paper-smooth-gan-sharp-smooth-2020.summary: This paper proposes SMOOTH-GAN, a conditional GAN with WGAN-GP loss for generating synthetic electronic health records such as laboratory values and medications conditioned on diagnosis codes, and demonstrates counterfactual reasoning to simulate co-occurring disease progression. The model is evaluated for statistical similarity and downstream machine learning prediction accuracy on EHR data. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list as prior work on modeling tabular data with conditional GANs, with no evidence it was run or adopted in the method.
paper-smooth-gan-sharp-smooth-2020.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is merely cited or actually run/compared as a baseline for synthetic EHR generation.

paper-prediction-method-rain-attenuation.summary: This paper proposes a new bivariate statistical model for predicting rain attenuation along millimeter-wave communication links, combining an effective path length model with a Weibull distribution to improve prediction accuracy over existing ITU-R methods. It is a telecommunications/propagation engineering study unrelated to synthetic data generation methodology. SDV's originating paper is cited only in passing to support the general claim that synthetic variables are commonly used in data analytics as substitutes for original variables.

paper-artificial-intelligence-society-20.summary: A wide-ranging OECD policy report examining the economic and social implications of artificial intelligence, covering topics such as AI adoption, labour markets, trust, and governance recommendations, and urging countries to move from AI principles to concrete action. The report cites the Synthetic Data Vault (Patki et al. 2016) somewhere in its extensive reference list, apparently in connection with synthetic data as a privacy or data-sharing technique, but no citing sentence or discussion is available in the evidence. The mention of SDV appears to be a passing citation rather than an engagement with or use of the library.

paper-generators-short-survey-techniques.summary: A survey paper cataloguing types of data generators used in software testing, machine learning, and other fields, categorizing them by architecture and intended use (e.g., randomizers, mathematical functions, noisers) and discussing pros, cons, and best practices. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited as an example of a general-purpose synthetic data generator built for scientific experiments, and its Gaussian Copula distribution is listed among the well-known distributions used by randomizer-type generators. SDV's Gaussian Copula concept is mentioned only in passing as one item in a survey list, with no implementation or experiment run.

paper-depth-behavior-modeling-transporta.summary: This paper presents conceptual work on a microsimulation model combining agent-based modeling and discrete event simulation to reproduce the complex behavior of a fictitious subway system, aiming to support decision-making on ridership prediction and delay management. Rather than using real data, the authors develop a toy model to simulate a wide variety of scenarios, citing the Synthetic Data Vault as a similar alternative approach to generating data without relying on hard-to-sample real system data. The SDV paper is cited only in passing as related prior work, not used or run in the study.

paper-collaborative-framework-tweaking-p.summary: This paper presents ASPECT, a demonstration framework for the 'Dataset Scaling Problem' in database benchmarking, which lets a user first scale a dataset's size with a tool S0 and then apply separate tools T1...Tn to enforce individual statistical properties in the resulting synthetic dataset, showing enforcement error and running time for each. It contrasts this modular approach with prior monolithic property-enforcement methods. SDV's original approach of extracting a property set from real data to generate a synthetic version is cited as one of several prior solutions to the scaling problem, but is not run or built upon.
paper-collaborative-framework-tweaking-p.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further beyond this single related-work citation, or verify author affiliations.

paper-contextual-anonymization-secondary.summary: This paper is a legal/ethics proposal offering an 'anonymization matrix' that adjusts anonymization standards for secondary use of biomedical big data according to data sensitivity and contextual safety factors, drawing on scoping review of law, ethics, and public attitudes research. It proposes a governance framework rather than a technical method, citing prior work on data anonymization and synthetic data techniques as background support. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing as an example of synthetic data substitution producing results similar to original data, with no method run.

preprint-accelerating-reproducible-resea.summary: This work introduces a lightweight, end-to-end benchmarking framework for synthetic Electronic Health Record generation, built on the PyHealth library, that unifies several longitudinal ICD-code generative baselines (MedGAN, CorGAN, PromptEHR, HALO, GPT-2) under a common data pipeline and evaluation suite. The authors state they integrate the sdmetrics library to provide standardized privacy-utility evaluation across methods, while also noting that SDV's sdmetrics framework is not directly applicable to the high dimensionality of ICD codes, prompting supplementary custom metrics. SDV's sdmetrics package is cited and partially integrated as one component of the paper's evaluation suite, run alongside bespoke discriminative and prevalence metrics rather than as the sole benchmarking tool.
preprint-accelerating-reproducible-resea.needs: The paper contains a contradiction: it claims to integrate sdmetrics for its evaluation suite in the contributions list, yet elsewhere states sdmetrics is not applicable to high-dimensional ICD codes. Unclear how much of the final evaluation actually runs sdmetrics versus custom metrics built instead of it.

preprint-amalgam-hybrid-llm-pgm-2026.summary: This preprint introduces Amalgam, a hybrid data-synthesis algorithm that combines a Probabilistic Graphical Model with an LLM, using PGM-derived summary statistics to condition zero-shot LLM sample generation for synthetic tabular/relational data with privacy and realism guarantees. The paper frames its contribution against two prior approaches, PGMs and Deep Learning models, citing CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) as an example of the latter category whose resulting data 'tends to capture a less accurate distribution.' CTGAN is only cited as prior deep-learning-based synthesis work, not run or benchmarked in the experiments.

preprint-class-dependent-hybrid-augmenta.summary: This paper reproduces and corrects prior migraine subtype classification studies for data leakage and metric bias, then proposes a class-dependent hybrid augmentation framework that assigns Gaussian Copula to small classes and CTGAN to larger classes, plus a 'fidelity asymmetry' concept for proportionally constrained synthetic growth. Evaluated on a 400-patient, seven/six-subtype clinical dataset with eight classifiers under stratified 5-fold cross-validation, the hybrid strategy outperforms single-method augmenters in macro-F1. SDV is run directly as the generator for both the Gaussian Copula and CTGAN synthesizers underpinning the entire augmentation pipeline, with CTGAN hyperparameters (epochs, batch_size, pac, generator_dim, discriminator_dim) also reported and TVAE included as an additional comparison generator.
preprint-class-dependent-hybrid-augmenta.needs: TVAE's synthesis library is not explicitly stated to be SDV (it may come from the separate ctgan/TVAE Python package); included as a named concept but its exact SDV provenance is unverified.

preprint-sae-discovering-steering-hierar.summary: This preprint introduces the Hybrid Hierarchical Sparse Autoencoder (HH-SAE), which factorizes complex manifolds into contextual, atomic, and compository tiers to resolve 'feature density conflict' in high-dimensional clinical and financial data, and uses the discovered hierarchy to steer synthetic data generation. In a cardiovascular-disease data-augmentation experiment with 1% class prevalence, the authors run CTGAN and TVAE as generative baselines alongside TabDiff, finding both degrade AUPRC relative to the original data while HH-SAE achieves a +9.9% lift. CTGAN and TVAE, from the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as comparison generators that the proposed method is shown to outperform.

preprint-repurposing-image-diffusion-mod.summary: This paper investigates whether an unmodified Stable Diffusion U-Net, originally built for image generation, can be repurposed to fabricate convincing tabular records by reshaping rows of the UCI Adult Income dataset into pseudo-images. It tests several feature-layout strategies and introduces the concept of 'ground truth drift,' distinguishing statistical from perceptual realism in adversarially generated synthetic data. CTGAN is cited only as prior work describing dedicated tabular generators, while SDMetrics is actually run throughout the evaluation pipeline to score statistical fidelity (column shape and pairwise-correlation scores) of the diffusion-generated tables, serving as one of several evaluation criteria alongside logic checks, downstream utility, and privacy disclosure tests.
preprint-repurposing-image-diffusion-mod.needs: cites_which_sdv_papers metadata lists only ctgan-neurips-2019, but the full text shows SDMetrics (an SDV-family package) actually run for evaluation without an explicit corresponding citation entry visible in the excerpts provided.

preprint-erp-provisioning-financial-cont.summary: This paper proposes SEQ-FCT, a governed ERP data-provisioning framework combining deterministic masking, synthetic scenario expansion, referential tokenization, and automated validation to support reconciliation, fraud-rule testing, and audit analytics without exposing production data. It is evaluated on a 186,000-record synthetic finance dataset against a production-clone upper bound, static masking, rules-only synthesis, a hybrid baseline, and a CTGAN-style generator, with SEQ-FCT reporting the strongest reconciliation F1, fraud recall, and lowest leakage risk. A 'CTGAN-style tabular generator' is run as one of several comparison baselines for synthetic scenario expansion, though it is unclear whether the actual CTGAN/SDV library was invoked or a custom reimplementation was used.
preprint-erp-provisioning-financial-cont.needs: Cannot confirm from evidence whether the paper actually ran the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an author-built 'CTGAN-style' reimplementation; no library name, import, or constructor parameters are given.

preprint-tracecodec-compiler-backed-neur.summary: This paper presents TraceCodec, a state-aware neural codec that lifts network packets into timed 'packet actions' with explicit flow slots and transport cues, learning continuous per-packet latents that a deterministic compiler lowers back into protocol-valid PCAPs. It shows that on CICIDS2017 and MAWI traces, TraceCodec preserves TCP state transitions, flow counts, and multi-flow interleaving far better than raw-field tabular generative baselines, which distort protocol state and fragment sessions. TVAE, originally introduced in the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper, is used as one of four raw-field baseline models, adapted and retrained on the packet-encoding task and evaluated against TraceCodec's compiler-backed decode interface.
preprint-tracecodec-compiler-backed-neur.needs: Not certain whether TVAE was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package's TVAE class or fully reimplemented from scratch; the custom training scripts and packet-action adaptation suggest a reimplementation (port) rather than direct library use, but this cannot be fully confirmed from the excerpted text.

paper-rule-guided-tabular-low-data-2025.summary: Targets tabular generation when only tens of reference rows exist, pairing a component that distils decision-tree logic into compact rules to guide a language model with a dual-granularity filter that screens generated rows at both the instance and the chunk level, and reports gains over both deep generative and prompt-based baselines at sample sizes from 30 to 500. CTGAN reaches the paper twice: it is named in related work as the classical method the paper departs from, faulted for mode collapse and heavy preprocessing, and it is the generator underneath the DRL constraint baseline, which the hyper-parameter table labels CTGAN-based and trains for 150 epochs at batch size 24.

preprint-reldiff-relational-generative-m.summary: RelDiff is a diffusion-based generative model for synthesizing complete relational databases that explicitly models the foreign-key graph structure, combining a graph-conditioned diffusion process for attributes with a Stochastic Block Model-based generator for structure. It is evaluated against prior relational synthesis methods on 11 benchmark datasets using fidelity, downstream-task, and privacy metrics. SDV is run as one of several baseline synthesizers in the comparison tables, and SDMetrics' Shape/Trend measures are adopted directly as the paper's fidelity metrics.

preprint-aigt-generative-table-prompt-20.summary: This paper proposes AIGT, a prompt-enhanced, LLM-based framework for synthesizing tabular data that leverages table metadata (descriptions and schemas) as prompts and uses long-token partitioning to scale to wide tables, evaluated on 20 public datasets plus two Alipay risk-control datasets. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of five state-of-the-art baseline synthesizers, trained for 300 epochs, and compared against AIGT on machine-learning-efficacy and data-quality metrics across many datasets. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE models are used as comparison baselines against which the proposed LLM-based generator is benchmarked, while a Gaussian copula model from the SDV paper is cited only descriptively as prior work.
preprint-aigt-generative-table-prompt-20.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN/TVAE were run via the sdv-dev package or an independent reimplementation; hyperparameter table shows only epoch counts, not sdv-specific constructor arguments, though training/sampling time table treats them as distinct runnable baselines.

preprint-constrained-adaptive-attack-eff.summary: This paper proposes CAPGD and CAA, new gradient-based and hybrid evasion attacks tailored to tabular deep learning models that respect feature relationship constraints, and shows they outperform prior attacks like CPGD and MOEVA across five architectures and four use cases. In their experiments, CT-GAN is considered as one of two data-augmentation techniques (alongside Cutmix) used to defend the tabular models being attacked. CTGAN is cited and applied only as an augmentation baseline against which the paper's attacks are evaluated, with no further engagement with its architecture.

preprint-difflm-controllable-synthetic-g.summary: This paper proposes DiffLM, a VAE-and-latent-diffusion framework that injects a learned latent representation of a target dataset into an LLM to generate controllable, high-quality structured synthetic data (tabular, code, tool data). It evaluates DiffLM against six baseline generators spanning GAN, VAE, diffusion, and LLM-based approaches on datasets like Adult, Default, Magic, Shoppers and Beijing, reporting MLE and correlation-distance metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of the six neural baselines against which DiffLM's synthetic tabular data quality is compared.

preprint-enhancing-quality-self-learning.summary: This paper introduces TriEnhance, a data-enhancement pipeline for imbalanced financial risk prediction (credit default and fraud detection) that combines adaptive synthetic sample generation, binary-feedback filtering, and self-learning with pseudo-labels, evaluated across six benchmark datasets. Within its data synthesis block, an adaptive algorithm selects between SMOTE and CTGAN based on F1 score to generate minority-class samples for augmentation. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is thus run as one of two candidate synthesis techniques automatically chosen per dataset rather than as the sole generator.

preprint-algorithm-drug-discovery-deep-2.summary: This preprint presents a multi-stage deep-learning pipeline for drug discovery, covering target identification via gene-expression analysis, prediction of drug-protein interactions, and IC50 prediction for candidate inhibitors, applied to an example of lung cancer therapy. To augment the patient gene-expression dataset used for target gene selection, the authors generate 50,000 synthetic patient records. The sdv library's CTGAN module is run as the generator producing this synthetic patient data that feeds the downstream feature-selection analysis.

preprint-disk-diffusion-model-structured.summary: This preprint introduces DiSK, a diffusion-based architecture for modeling heterogeneous structured/tabular data (text, categorical, numerical fields), aimed at improved tabular synthesis and imputation compared to autoregressive language models and existing tabular generative approaches. The authors benchmark DiSK against TabDDPM, CTAB-GAN, CTAB-GAN+, SMOTE, and TVAE across more than 15 diverse datasets. TVAE, cited to Xu et al. 2019 (the CTGAN paper), is run as one of several baseline generative models the new method is compared against in the tabular synthesis experiments.

paper-distvae-distributional-2023.summary: Attacks the Gaussianity assumption in variational autoencoders by replacing the reconstruction term with a continuous ranked probability score, so that the decoder estimates conditional quantiles and the model learns the full distribution rather than reconstructing points, with theorems showing the objective recovers the ground-truth distribution. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the three generators DistVAE is benchmarked against across six tabular datasets, on machine-learning utility, correlation structure, marginal similarity, distance to closest record and attribute disclosure, with per-model hyperparameters and parameter counts reported.

preprint-deep-ensemble-uncertainty-quant.summary: This preprint develops DCRNN-SQRUQ, a scalable deep-ensemble uncertainty quantification method for a diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network used in short-term traffic forecasting, combining simultaneous quantile regression with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and generative modeling to build diverse ensembles. To generate new high-performing hyperparameter configurations for the ensemble, the authors fit a multivariate Gaussian copula model to top configurations found via hyperparameter search and sample new ones from it. SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer (SDV package v0.14.0) is run directly as the generative model that produces the sampled hyperparameter configurations underlying the ensemble construction.

preprint-fairgen-fair-synthetic-generati.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-architecture-agnostic pipeline that removes bias-inducing samples from training data before synthetic data generation, aiming to reduce fairness disparities without redesigning any specific GAN. The pipeline is evaluated on the Adult Income and German Credit datasets across three generator architectures, comparing raw generation, a k%-removal preprocessing technique, and data augmentation. CTGAN and a 'Gaussian Copula GAN' (cited to Patki et al., 2016, the SDV paper) are run as two of the three generator architectures the fairness pipeline is tested on, alongside a separately-cited 'Copula GAN' from Kamthe et al.'s copula flows work.
preprint-fairgen-fair-synthetic-generati.needs: The paper's 'Gaussian Copula GAN' is cited to Patki et al. 2016 (SDV), suggesting SDV's GaussianCopula synthesizer, while a separately-listed 'Copula GAN' is cited to Kamthe et al.'s unrelated copula flows paper -- naming may not exactly track sdv-dev's CopulaGAN synthesizer; treated here as SDV's GaussianCopula per the citation.

preprint-balancing-thermal-comfort-datas.summary: This paper investigates class-balancing techniques for imbalanced thermal-comfort survey datasets and proposes comfortGAN, a modified conditional GAN, comparing it against SMOTE, ADASYN, TGAN, and CTGAN across three public thermal comfort datasets. The results show comfortGAN generally improves downstream classification accuracy more than the other augmentation methods, though gains shrink when classes are merged. TGAN and CTGAN (the SDV-family tabular GAN models) are run unmodified as baseline data generators, with TGAN's hyperparameters tuned via its sdv-dev GitHub search tool, and both are benchmarked against the authors' proposed comfortGAN.

paper-multi-stage-disentangled-2020.summary: Splits disentangled representation learning into two stages, a penalty-based model that infers independent factors and a second conditional model that recovers the correlated residual, so reconstruction quality is regained without weakening disentanglement, and shows the construction can be realised with variational autoencoders, adversarial networks or normalising flows. A closing section carries the method to simulated credit tabular data, where TVAE is one of two benchmark generators trained against it and its mode-specific normalization is set out as the reference treatment of mixed continuous and discrete columns.

preprint-gain-pseudo-label-conditional-2.summary: This paper proposes PC-GAIN, an unsupervised missing-data imputation method that extends GAIN by pre-training an auxiliary classifier on pseudo-labels derived from low-missing-rate data and incorporating it into the adversarial imputation framework, improving imputation quality over GAIN and other baselines. It cites TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) only in its reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

preprint-synthesizing-tabular-generative.summary: Introduces Tabular GAN (TGAN), a generative adversarial network that generates fully synthetic tabular data with mixed discrete and continuous columns, and shows it outperforms conventional statistical generative models on three datasets. The paper is the founding work for the 'tgan' component of the SDV family, authored by the MIT DAI Lab researchers behind SDV, and its citation of the earlier SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) situates TGAN within that same synthetic-data ecosystem rather than reporting any use of SDV's software.
